motivation: Test whether retaining non-Thalassia seagrass at an exact meter mark during a one-year Thalassia non-detection predicts higher next-year Thalassia recorded return than becoming seagrass-bare.

source.stable_point_id: Point-event locationID constructed upstream as Transect + Site/meter-mark identity
source.seagrass_definition: Present occurrence rows in order Alismatales
source.point_year_consistency: Retain only point-years for which repeated visits agree on the complete present-Alismatales taxon set.

three_year_sequence.exclusion: Loss year 2016 is excluded prospectively because the 2016/2017 recorded-state pulse has an independently documented protocol sensitivity.

groups.loss_year_other_seagrass: Thalassia absent at t and >=1 other Alismatales taxon present at t
groups.loss_year_bare: Thalassia absent at t and no present Alismatales taxon at t

endpoint: Thalassia present at t+1 at the same stable meter mark (recorded return; not demographic recolonization)

hypothesis.statement: Thalassia recorded return one year after exact-point loss is more frequent when another seagrass remains at the loss-year point than when the point becomes seagrass-bare.
hypothesis.estimator: risk difference P(return | other seagrass at loss year) - P(return | bare at loss year)
hypothesis.support_rule: lower bound of 95% node-cluster bootstrap interval for risk difference > 0

secondary_descriptive.by_segment: Report return fractions separately for Old, Middle, and Lower Tampa Bay; do not promote a segment-specific result if pooled primary support fails.
secondary_descriptive.by_loss_year_taxon: Among loss-year occupied points, report which alternative taxa were present and their observed return fractions; descriptive only.
secondary_descriptive.sensitivity_2016: Report 2016 loss-year sequences separately as protocol-sensitive context; they cannot replace the primary 2017-2024 result.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc ecological hypothesis motivated by the supported community-insurance result.
A positive association would identify a recovery-scaffold candidate, not prove facilitation or causal enhancement of Thalassia recovery.
Recorded return is observation-state reappearance at a re-observed exact point, not demographic recolonization.
Persistent favorable habitat could jointly explain alternative-seagrass retention and Thalassia return.
Do not restore loss year 2016 to the primary endpoint, lower event/node minima, change the segment pool, or redefine bare/occupied after opening the result.
